nodes.description: Premature GnRH pulsatility activates pituitary gonadotrophs to secrete LH and FSH, which stimulate the gonads to produce sex steroids (estradiol in girls, testosterone in boys). The resulting premature gonadarche drives early development of secondary sexual characteristics, accelerated linear growth, and advanced skeletal maturation that can compromise adult height.

evidence.reference_title: Central precocious puberty: From genetics to treatment.
evidence.snippet:
Central precocious puberty (CPP) results from early activation of the 
hypothalamic - pituitary -gonadal (HPG) axis and follows the same sequence as 
normal puberty.

nodes.description: Kisspeptin, the product of KISS1, is the excitatory input for the secretion of GnRH, and it acts through the G-protein-coupled receptor KISS1R (previous symbol GPR54). Variants that raise the tone of this input cause CPP from the stimulatory side rather than by releasing an inhibitory brake, and the reported KISS1R Arg386Pro receptor produces a longer intracellular signal than normal for the same kisspeptin exposure.

nodes.description: Long-acting GnRH agonists (e.g., leuprolide) are first-line therapy for CPP. Continuous (non-pulsatile) GnRH receptor stimulation desensitizes pituitary gonadotrophs, suppressing LH/FSH and sex-steroid secretion, halting pubertal progression and preserving adult height potential.

nodes.description: MKRN3 and DLK1 are both expressed only from the paternal allele, and both act to hold the hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator quiescent through childhood. Hypothalamic Mkrn3 transcript is abundant in the arcuate nucleus of prepubertal mice and falls immediately before puberty, so withdrawal of this brake is part of the normal pubertal trigger. A paternally transmitted loss-of-function variant in either gene removes the brake before the normal age of puberty; in the family in which the DLK1 defect was found, the deletion removed the DLK1 translational start site and left circulating DLK1 undetectable in every affected member.
nodes.id: Loss of Paternally Expressed Imprinted Restraint on the GnRH Pulse Generator

evidence.reference_title: A GPR54-activating mutation in a patient with central precocious puberty.
evidence.snippet:
Gonadotropin-dependent, or central, precocious puberty is caused by early 
maturation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis. In girls, this condition 
is most often idiopathic.

nodes.description: The central event in CPP is premature reawakening of the hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator. Hypothalamic GnRH neurons resume high-amplitude pulsatile GnRH secretion before the normal age of puberty, driving pituitary gonadotropin release. Upstream kisspeptin (KISS1/KISS1R) signaling stimulates GnRH neurons, while inhibitory factors including the paternally expressed imprinted genes MKRN3 and DLK1 normally restrain the axis during childhood; loss of this restraint or gain of kisspeptin tone triggers premature secretion.

hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis results in central precocious puberty.
